chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: Charlie Barnet's reorganized band of 1948
summary: Leeman rejoins Barnet's new band, suggests Eddie Safranski from Kenton's band and records with it for six or seven months.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: First, when I came off from the Glen Gray band, Charlie Barnet reorganized in '48 and I was with that new band, and he didn't know who to hire, among other things -- he was groping around for musicians, and I mentioned Stan Kenton's first big band had broken up, and they were well known in all the polls and everything, you know, I had suggested Eddie Sefranski; he got him.
And he had a couple of the arrangers -- oh, I can't think of their names. Out in Hollywood, he got ...
Well, Ralph originally was in Louie's Woody's
band, and I got Chubby Jackson his job. I have all these things down.
Well, you don't have them all down here.
But you go back and forth, you know, and ...
You go back and forth. I'm telling you to do whatever you want to do.
Well, Barnet had a new Martin band, with some of the Kenton arrangements, and I was with that and recorded with them, I was only with them about six or seven months.
Now what year is that you're talking about, Cliff?
This was right after I came back from Texas with Gray.
